content.text: A criminal conviction has the potential to completely change the rest of your life. If you or a loved one have recently been charged with a crime in Ventura County or the greater Los Angeles, CA area, it’s essential to know how an experienced Los Angeles criminal defense lawyer can assist your situation. Whether you’re being charged with a crime for the first time, or you have a criminal record of past offenses, a conviction could mean fines, time behind bars, and various other penalties. The right defense attorney can make a significant difference in the outcome of your criminal case in Los Angeles or Ventura County. The Law Offices of James E. Silverstein is a full-service criminal defense firm representing clients throughout Ventura County and the greater Los Angeles area. The right attorney will ensure your rights are protected and that you have the best possible chance of achieving a favorable outcome in your case. Here are some tips for choosing the right criminal defense attorney: Choose a criminal lawyer who is experienced in handling your specific type of case.If you have been accused of a crime, it is important to choose an attorney who has the direct experience and education in handling your type of case. The right attorney will be familiar with the laws that apply to your situation and will be able to give you the best possible defense. You should be able to reach your attorney when you need to, and you should feel confident that your attorney is working on your case. The right attorney will have a history of winning California criminal cases and will be able to provide you with the best possible defense. Having the ability to leverage best practices from past cases is critical to success. Know Your Rights After a California Arrest Every American citizen has constitutional rights that come into play during an arrest for any criminal offense. Additionally, every American also has civil rights intended to prevent them from experiencing unjust mistreatment at the hands of law enforcement. The police may not treat suspects differently based on their individual characteristics, and they must always uphold the laws of due process when conducting arrests and booking procedures. The two most important rights you have during an arrest are provided by the Fifth and Sixth Amendments of the United States Constitution. The Fifth Amendment provides protection from self-incrimination. This means an individual accused of a crime has the right to remain silent during an arrest. When the police arrest a suspect for a criminal offense, they must read the suspect their Miranda rights, which includes an explanation of their right to remain silent and the fact that anything they say can be used against them in court. It’s vital to exercise this right and politely comply with police. Say nothing to the police until you have secured legal representation from a Los Angeles criminal defense attorney. The Sixth Amendment provides the right to legal representation in a criminal case. Every American accused of a crime has the right to an attorney, even if they cannot afford to hire one or do not wish to incur the expense of hiring a private defense attorney. Public defenders are available to anyone accused of a crime at no charge. These court-appointed defense lawyers can provide legal representation to suspects who cannot afford to hire private attorneys. However, if you have the means to do so, it is worth hiring an experienced private Los Angeles defense attorney. While most public defenders are capable defense lawyers, they have very busy schedules and often cannot provide clients with much individual attention. What Cases Can a Los Angeles and Ventura County Defense Lawyer Handle? The Law Offices of James E. Silverstein has years of experience guiding clients through a wide range of criminal cases. We can provide comprehensive defense counsel for all types of criminal charges, including: Violent crime cases. Violent crimes like assault, armed robbery, and homicide are some of the most harshly punished criminal offenses in California. If you have been charged with any type of violent crime, you could face years behind bars if convicted. Drug offense cases. California has some of the most relaxed drug laws in the country, but that doesn’t mean a drug charge won’t interfere with your life in many ways. Attorney James E. Silverstein can help you avoid the harshest penalties possible in your drug offense case. White-collar crime cases. Business-related crimes of fraud and deception may not be violent, but they are incredibly destructive to the lives of the victims. Our team can handle the most complex financial crime cases, helping you determine your most viable defenses. Sex crime cases. California prosecutors tend to pursue conviction in sex crime cases very aggressively, and conviction could mean lifetime registration as a sex offender, among other penalties. We can also help you remove your name from lifetime sexual offenders registry based on new laws. DUI cases. Driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol is very dangerous for the impaired driver and everyone around them. These cases are some of the most commonly prosecuted criminal cases in California, and conviction can mean a loss of driving privileges, fines, and incarceration. These are only a few examples of the types of cases your defense team can handle when you choose the Law Offices of James E. Silverstein to represent you. What Is a DUI? How Can a Criminal Defense Lawyer Defend a DUI Charge? A DUI is a criminal offense that occurs when a person drives while under the influence of alcohol or drugs. The penalties for a DUI depend on the circumstances of the offense, but they can range from a misdemeanor to a felony. A DUI can result in jail time, probation, and a driver’s license suspension. A Los Angeles DUI can also result in a higher insurance rate and difficulty getting a job. However, it’s important to note that not all DUIs are treated equally. The severity of the offense and the penalties depend on factors such as the blood alcohol content (BAC), the presence of drugs in the system, the type of vehicle being driven, and whether there were any accidents or injuries. On occasion, people are unfairly charged with a DUI. This happens in situations where: The police officer did not have probable cause to stop the driver. The field sobriety tests were not conducted properly. The breathalyzer test was not administered properly. The driver was not actually under the influence of alcohol or drugs. In these situations, a skilled and experienced criminal defense and DUI attorney can help you fight the DUI charge by challenging the evidence against you. A Los Angeles criminal defense lawyer can also negotiate with the prosecutor to get the charges reduced or dismissed and ensure that your innocence is preserved. What Evidence Can Be Used In a Criminal Defense Case? In a criminal defense case in Los Angeles, CA, the attorney will review all the evidence to determine if there are any holes or ways to attack it. The evidence that can be used in a criminal defense case includes: The police report: The police report includes the officer’s account of what happened and any statements that were made by the accused. Sometimes, the officer’s account can be inaccurate or misleading. This can be used to create doubt about the prosecutor’s case. The arresting officer’s testimony: The arresting officer will testify about what happened during the arrest. This can be used to challenge the officer’s account of events. Witness testimony: Witnesses who saw what happened can provide valuable information that can be used to support the defense and counter the prosecution’s case. Physical evidence: Physical evidence can include things like blood tests, DNA evidence, and fingerprints. This evidence can be used to support the defense if it is accurate and properly collected. Photographs and Video: Photographs and video evidence can be used to show what happened and challenge the prosecution’s version of events. What Are the Different Types of Criminal Defenses? There are many different types of criminal defenses that can be used in a criminal case. The type of defense that is used depends on the facts of the case and the evidence that is available. Some of the most common types of defenses include: Alibi: An alibi defense is where the accused can prove that they were not at the scene of the crime. This can be done with witness testimony, video evidence, or other documentation. Self-defense: A self-defense claim can be used when the accused can show that they were acting in self-defense when the crime occurred. This defense can be used when the accused was threatened with violence or feared for their life. Mistaken identity: A mistaken identity defense can be used when the accused can show that they were not the person who committed the crime. This can be done through different forms of physical and eyewitness evidence. Improper police procedure: This defense can be used when the accused can show that the police did not follow proper procedure when they were arrested or when they collected evidence. This can be used to suppress evidence that was improperly obtained. Insanity: An insanity defense can be used when the accused can show that they were not in their right mind when the crime occurred. This can be due to mental illness or intoxication. Coercion: A coercion defense can be used when the accused can show that they were forced to commit the crime. This can be through threats of violence or other forms of coercion. Ultimately, there are several avenues to explore with a criminal defense attorney by your side. Any number of these defense positions have already been used to great success in court. The key is working with an attorney you trust to investigate every possibility and build the strongest case possible on your behalf. Tips for Anyone Who Has Been Accused of Crimes in LA, California If you have been accused of a crime in Los Angeles County, it is important to take the accusation seriously and seek out legal help as soon as possible. The sooner you start working with a criminal defense attorney, the better. Here are some tips for anyone who has been accused of a crime: Do not talk to the police: It is important to exercise your legal right to keep silent when being questioned by the police. Anything that you choose to say can be used against you in court. Do not post on social media: Anything that you post on social media can be used against you in court. It is important to avoid posting anything online regarding the case. Do not talk to witnesses: It is important to let your attorney handle any contact with witnesses. Talking to witnesses can be tricky, and it is best to leave it to the professionals. Do not miss court: It is important to show up for all court appearances. Missing court can result in a warrant being issued for your arrest. Do not give up: It is important to remember that you are innocent until proven guilty. Never give up, and always fight for your innocence with your attorney by your side. These are just a few of the things that you should keep in mind if you have been accused of a crime. If you have been accused of a crime, the best thing that you can do is to seek out legal help as soon as possible. A criminal defense attorney will be able to help you navigate the legal system and fight for your innocence. How Much Do Criminal Defense Attorneys Cost? The total amount of money that you will spend on a criminal defense attorney will depend on several factors. The severity of the charge, the amount of time that is needed to prepare the case, and the location of the court are just a few of the factors that will affect the cost. In general, it’s best to connect directly with an attorney to discuss pricing, as it can vary greatly. While the overall cost can intimate some, the long-term financial and personal costs will far outweigh the initial investment in securing legal help. What to Expect From a Ventura County and Los Angeles Criminal Defense Attorney Regardless of your criminal history, it’s understandable to feel distressed and uncertain in the face of any criminal charge in Los Angeles or Ventura County. The outcome of your case has the potential to affect your life in several ways for years to come, and approaching this situation with confidence is much easier when you have an experienced Los Angeles criminal defense lawyer on your side. The Law Offices of James E. Silverstein will begin handling your case with a comprehensive review of the situation that led to your arrest, including all available evidence and the police report from the incident. We’ll make sure the police followed due process in handling your arrest and booking. Once we have a firm grasp of the situation, we’ll help you determine the best available defenses. Many criminal cases are successfully defended by proving mistaken identity or self-defense. It’s also possible to beat criminal charges on procedural grounds when police or prosecutors mishandle evidence or make other mistakes with their cases. Our team can help you gather evidence that disproves the prosecution’s evidence, prepare you for each phase of your proceedings, and help you mitigate penalties through plea bargaining if conviction is unavoidable. If you or a loved one are charged with a crime in Los Angeles or Ventura County, you will have the chance to make phone calls after you complete booking. Make sure one of those calls is to a Los Angeles criminal defense attorney you can trust. If you need guidance for an upcoming criminal case in Los Angeles or Ventura County, contact the Law Offices of James E. Silverstein and schedule a consultation with our team.
